items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: then come Bailey and Derby, the dancers, two dancers, So, man, them cats could lay some wood, they could dance.

ctx.x: The curtain broke, and the spot's on me and all you can is my face and my hands, hitting anything. I don't know whether it was right or wrong. Just making some noise. Man, about the eighth bar, they stood up, standing ovation. They hadn't seen the whole band yet. Stood up, cheers.

Cheers, youhear me? No exaggeration. I'm telling you like it was. Cheers. They got through the first number, then come Bailey and Derby, the dancers, two dancers, So, man, them cats could lay some wood, they could dance. So they come out and done their act and broke it up. So they act -- and me, I had never done that before, everytime they come out, I threw

arpeggio on the tympani, pedal--on tympani you know. That's what they call milking. I scared them half to death, so when they come off and we done that, everyone -- Ivie come up, naturally we killed them, and we closed our act with "Mood Indigo". Tricky and Barney and Lawrence -- no, Tricky -- who was it -- it was Tricky and Lawrence Brown and Carney come down and played just plain sweet melody and I was singing with the band then. And I was singing a high obbligato in back of it. It was faint, haunting, you…
